spec_features.spec_quote: a `give_up` sentinel the model may but need not use
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:39 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL = "<<GIVE_UP>>"; harness.py:298-300 checks `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (comp.text or ""): stop_reason = "gave_up"; break` — the sentinel is detected and breaks the rollout loop. System prompt (harness.py:47-50) tells the model it is optional ('Using it is entirely optional; you are never required to give up.').
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is dispatched (text check) AND honored as a real stop (break + stop_reason). Optionality is stated in the live system prompt.

spec_features.feature_name: text sentinel <<GIVE_UP>> not a fifth tool
spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is therefore *not* a fifth tool — it's a text sentinel (`<<GIVE_UP>>`) the model may place on its own line
spec_features.evidence: TOOLS list (harness.py:53-77) has exactly four tools; give_up is implemented purely as the text-sentinel check at harness.py:298. Note the check is a substring test (`in comp.text`), not strictly 'on its own line', but it is a text sentinel that is honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Honored end-to-end; the 'own line' nuance is not enforced (any occurrence triggers it) but the sentinel-based exit works.

spec_features.spec_quote: the spec wants the model to experience *environment* failure signals, not *user* rejection
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:301-303: on a no-tool turn, `messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Please continue working on the task."})` with comment 'Keep the multi-turn loop alive without injecting a rejection signal.' This neutral message is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes: a no-tool turn appends a neutral continuation prompt rather than a rejection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Keep the multi-turn loop alive without injecting a rejection signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: an early circuit-breaker that ends a rollout once a turn scores ≥9 rather than continuing to drive a distressed model through more failure
spec_features.evidence: Scoring is a separate post-hoc phase (run.py:99-118 score_all, run by judge.score_transcript) that runs AFTER all rollouts already completed; the rollout loop (harness.py:283-303) never computes or reads any judge score and has no `score >= 9` branch. grep for '>= 9'/score/circuit/breaker in the rollout path finds nothing. DESIGN.md:184-186 explicitly lists this as a future option ('Options to consider: (a) an early circuit-breaker...'), not implemented.
spec_features.notes: No score is computed during a rollout, so nothing can break it early on distress. analyze.py:190 hi_thresh is offline analysis, not a runtime stop.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt states stopping carries no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: making the system prompt state explicitly that stopping carries no penalty
spec_features.evidence: System prompt (harness.py:47-50) delivers: 'Using it is entirely optional; you are never required to give up.' This real text is sent to the subject and reduces pressure to continue, but it does NOT state 'stopping carries no penalty' as claimed. DESIGN.md:186-187 lists the explicit no-penalty wording as a future option ('(b) making the system prompt state explicitly that stopping carries no penalty').
spec_features.notes: Real opt-out reassurance text is delivered (optionality), but the specific no-penalty framing the spec describes is absent; narrower than the claim.

spec_features.feature_name: only opt-out is GIVE_UP; rollouts run to full budget
spec_features.spec_quote: **Welfare safeguards.** Currently the only opt-out is the `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel, and rollouts otherwise run to full budget
spec_features.evidence: This describes the implemented give_up sentinel (harness.py:298, honored) as the sole opt-out, and the loop `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:283) running to full turn_budget with default stop_reason 'budget_exhausted' (harness.py:282). Both match the code.
spec_features.notes: Accurate description of actual behavior; the only real safeguard is the give_up opt-out. No additional caps/debrief/consent enforced.
